tier_reason: The README's 'Comparisons With Other Compressors' section gives first-party timings against smaz (0.325s vs 0.145s) and gzip/xz (table) measured 'on my computer' with no CPU, compiler or run count; the committed test_input.c and shoco-bin.c cover only the shoco side and no smaz harness exists, so the evidence is first-party with partial methodology (tier C).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README timings; the repo Makefile builds with $(CC) -std=c99 -O3 -Wall plus user CFLAGS, and the README says it was only tested with gcc/clang on x86_64 Linux.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers measured 'on my computer' (README, 2014): no CPU, compiler, flags or OS version stated, no run count. The smaz row has no committed harness; the shoco 0.145s figure equals the 'user' time of the README's own test_input example on /usr/share/dict/words (479,828 lines), and test_input.c times fgets input, compress, decompress and a strcmp check per line, so the two sides may not have been timed the same way. The gzip/xz table times whole processes of the shoco-bin command-line tool, which compresses the 4.95 MB file in one call including file I/O; the README calls whole-file use 'not a strong point of shoco', gzip/xz levels are not stated, and gzip/xz reach far better ratios (1.48 MB and 1.23 MB vs 3.39 MB), so that comparison is not like for like. The baseline is not a C++ standard facility. The numbers predate the March 2015 'Prevent buffer overflows in decompression' fix and the December 2015 end-of-string fix. Open issue #28 (2017, unanswered) reports an AFL/AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read in shoco_decompress() on malformed input (24 bytes before chrs_by_chr_and_successor_id), so decompressing untrusted data is unsafe; open issue #35 reports some ASCII strings (e.g. 'My-Nam3-iZ-H@5eeB-M33R') failing to compress. The README begins 'This project is unmaintained. You should use ZStandard nowadays'; the last code change is the 2015-12-08 merge of pull request #17, and the 2026-02-16 commit only marks the project unmaintained. No independent speed benchmark of the C library against smaz was found (a search surfaced only ratio comparisons by Unishox2 and a third-party smaz speed-up blog). The README's '/usr/dict/share/words' path is the author's typo for /usr/share/dict/words.

notes: Numbers in claimed_speedup match the README exactly and the derived ratios are labelled correctly; tier C stands. Main shortcomings to record: no hardware/compiler for the timings, no smaz harness, gzip/xz row is a whole-file CLI comparison against much stronger compressors, and an open unfixed global-buffer-overflow read in shoco_decompress (issue #28) on malformed input. MIT license confirmed from LICENSE; not archived, not a fork; abandoned per the author's README note despite the 2026-02-16 notice commit.
